newsitem.title: BULGARIA: France for equal E.Euro access to EU, NATO - Bulgaria.
newsitem.headline: France for equal E.Euro access to EU, NATO - Bulgaria.

text.p: France supports giving equal treatment to East European success stories and to their less economically developed neighbours when they seek full European Union and NATO membership, Bulgaria's premier said on Sunday.

Interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski said on return from a visit to Paris that France also supported Bulgaria's application for a rescheduling of its debt to the Paris Club of government creditors.
"France categorically will support equal treatment and equal access for all ex-socialist countries," he told reporters at Sofia airport.

NATO member countries are to hold a summit in Madrid in July to nominate the first candidates for membership from post-communist countries, and diplomats have said Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic are most likely to be named.

The EU has promised Bulgaria and nine other former East bloc countries -- Poland, Hungary, the Czech Republic, Slovakia, Slovenia, Romania, Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania -- eventual membership, but they are not expected to be admitted all at once.

Sofianski said last week he had asked the Paris Club to roll over up to $50 million of this year's dues. Bulgaria has so far paid these amounts regularly, but an economic crisis caused by continuous mishandling of the economy has depleted its reserves.
Sofianski said French Prime Minister Alain Juppe had promised him France would use its influence with the International Monetary Fund and with the Paris Club to help Bulgaria win new agreements.

Sofianski, who was in Paris for a meeting of the European Democratic Union, said French financial institutions had shown interest in Bulgaria's debt problems, and also in concrete projects, specifically in the field of natural gas.
He said he expected to receive proposals soon, but declined to give more details.
